newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Innogenetics says could spin off successful units.
newsitem.headline: Innogenetics says could spin off successful units.

text.p: Belgian biotech firm Innogenetics NV, which on Tuesday became the first company to seek a listing on Europe's new Easdaq small cap market, said in the future it could spin off and separately quote successful units.
"Belgium has lots of financial holding companies. We could become the first scientific holding," Innogenetics chief executive officer Hugo Van Heuverswyn told Reuters.
"I strongly believe Innogenetics is the core of a group of companies," Van Heuverswyn.
One of the first candidates for future growth as a standalone company was Innogenetics' skin and tissue repair division.
It had several products in clinical trials which if successful would be grouped and held by a separate company.
"This could be a vehicle for joint ventures or to raise finance (via a listing) for phase three clinical trials," he said.
Innogenetics' wound healing division would yield the first therapeutic products, he said. Others would follow from its immune therapy research.
This would help move the company away from being reliant on revenues from its diagnostic tests for diseases such as HIV and Alzheimer's.
Innogenetics presently sells 11 such tests. Twenty eight more, including tests for diseases such as tuberculosis, are due to be brought to market over the next three years.
